newsitem.title: USA: Plainfield, N.J., gets reprieve on budget -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Plainfield, N.J., gets reprieve on budget -- paper.

text.p: New Jersey has given Plainfield officials more time to come up with a new budget, allowing city officials to work on the plan until the end of January, the Star Ledger reported Wednesday.

Last week, the state ordered the city to adopt a final 1998 budget by Friday, or face fines. But after the city failed to schedule hearings or a final vote on the budget, which is four months overdue, the state agreed not to enforce the fines until the end of the month.
State officials said the reprieve is contingent on Plainfield getting going on budget deliberations. Work sessions on the budget are now set for Thursday and Saturday, the paper said.

Plainfield is one of eleven communities in the state that have still not adopted fiscal 1998 budgets. The others are Bayonne, Camden, Elizabeth, Irvington, Jersey City, Lodi, North Brunswick, Orange, Passaic and Paterson.
